title: House of Hohenstaufen
capsule: The Hohenstaufen dynasty ruled the Holy Roman Empire from 1138, reaching its zenith under Frederick I Barbarossa (r. 1155–1190) and Frederick II (r. 1220–1250), who simultaneously held the German, Sicilian, Burgundian, and Jerusalem crowns and issued the landmark Constitutions of Melfi (1231). After Frederick II's death the line collapsed rapidly: Conrad IV died in 1254, and Conradin — the last legitimate male heir — led an Italian campaign to recover Sicily but was captured by Charles of Anjou and publicly executed in Naples on 29 October 1268, extinguishing the dynasty. The geometric window 1260–1272 covers the contested interregnum from Conradin's claims through to Rudolf of Habsburg's election in 1273.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty's territorial control is well documented through imperial and papal records; the 1260–1272 window captures only the final contested phase under Conradin rather than the dynasty at full power.
